Decisions

What the demo claims

Afterlife finds a part-and-lot cohort whose claim rate jumped, shows the data behind it, and drafts a supplier brief for a person to review. It does not claim that monthly supplier shares prove a supplier is liable for each individual claim.

Ingestion

CSV extracts plus the SAP adapter. No live connectors. check.py is a hard stop: any failed check blocks the run.

Row-level quarantine (load the good rows, hold the bad ones) is a production feature, not a demo one. Adapter tests already cover PO-line IDs, zero-padded numbers, decimal commas and price units.

OwnerSpend thread
Claim → part links

A link is a suggestion with evidence and a confidence score. Alerts use links at confidence 0.5 and above. Recovery uses only links at the recovery threshold or confirmed by a person.

Recovery threshold = the lowest confidence that reaches 99% precision on holdout data. On spend links that is 0.8 today; claim links get their own number once match_claims is built.

OwnerWarranty thread
Supplier attribution

Supplier shares estimate a cohort's exposure. A single claim is assigned to a supplier only when its product-month used one supplier's lot. Claims from mixed months are labeled supplier unresolved and shown with their count and cost.

Production use needs serial-to-batch records (which lot went into which unit). We name that as a data requirement.

OwnerWarranty thread
Early warning

An alert triggers an investigation; it doesn't accuse anyone. Rule: mature build months only, at least 2 baseline months, rate ratio ≥ 1.5, at least 10 claims after the step, and Benjamini–Hochberg q < 0.05 across every part-supplier series tested. Each alert shows its denominators and q-value.

A build month counts as mature once its 3 months in service plus the typical reporting lag have passed.

Reviews before a supplier is namedSupplier quality engineer
Cost

Warranty cost = parts + labor + other cost, counted once. Service purchases for warranty repairs reconcile against claims and are never added. Lifecycle cost on the Overview = build cost + spare-part purchases + gross warranty cost. Net warranty cost (gross minus settled recoveries) is shown beside it, not instead of it.

Signs off reconciliationFinance
Agreement terms

A person reviews every agreement once before its terms value any recovery. Amended clauses, missing fields and low-confidence values are flagged for that review.

Stricter than reviewing only flagged fields, and still cheap: a supplier has one agreement, and it's reused for every claim.

ReviewsProcurement
Supplier brief

Always a draft. It keeps four levels of evidence apart: observed claims, inferred part links, cohort exposure for the supplier, and claims individually attributable to the supplier. Only the last level can enter a recovery submission.

OwnersSupplier quality (technical), procurement (negotiation), warranty recovery manager (submission), finance (books)
Dates

Time in service counts from the build month. That's a stated demo limitation; production needs the retail sale or registration date. Filing deadlines count from paid_date, which v4 provides.

OwnerWarranty thread

Seal kit 200-1180-01 · builds April–June 2026

Which supplier made the failed part?

build_supply records supplier shares per product and month, not per unit. That's enough to measure a cohort's claim rate. It identifies the supplier of one failed part only when the product-month used a single supplier's lot.

UV-400
Keystone 100%
20 claims · $5,158.94
Attributable to Keystone
TR-250
Keystone 100%
38 claims · $9,505.84
Attributable to Keystone
UV-600
Keystone 50%Bluewater 50%
16 claims · $3,970.28
Supplier unresolved

58 of the 74 seal-kit claims from these builds (78%, $14,664.78) can be tied to Keystone. All 74 count toward the cohort claim rate.

Alerts: cohort level
  • Claim rate per supplier uses single-supplier months first
  • Mixed months are separated by subtracting the other supplier's known rate
  • Exposure is labeled as a cohort estimate
Recovery: claim level
  • Only claims from single-supplier product-months
  • Mixed-month claims stay supplier unresolved, with count and cost shown
  • Production fix: serial-to-batch records
Unstructured data · AI extraction

Supplier documents and the terms we extract

Each production supplier has one agreement in supplier_agreements/. The extractor turns each document into one row of terms, and every value quotes the clause it came from.

supplier_agreements/sqa_keystone-seal-works.md
Supplier Quality Agreement

Prairie Utility Vehicles ("Buyer") and Keystone Seal Works, supplier no. S-022supplier_id ("Supplier"), MX. Effective 2025-01-01.

4. Quality

4.1 Supplier maintains IATF 16949 certification and ships with a certificate of conformance per lot.

7. Warranty

7.1 Supplier warrants each part for 18 months from the date of manufacturewindow of the end unit in which it is installed.

7.2 For field failures attributable to Supplier's parts, Supplier reimburses 100% of parts and dealer labor, labor at the hours actually claimed and capped at USD 90 per hour.

7.3 Recovery claims are submitted within 90 days after Buyer pays the dealer claim.

7.4 Freight, handling and administrative fees are not recoverable.

Amendment No. 1 (effective 2025-06-01)

Sections 7.2 and 7.3 are replaced as follows. Supplier reimburses 80%recovery_pct of parts and dealer laborlabor_covered, labor at the hours actually claimed and capped at USD 90 per hourlabor_rate_cap. Recovery claims must be submitted within 45 days after Buyer pays the dealer claimfiling_deadline; late claims are void. All other terms are unchanged.

Extraction rules

Every value quotes its clauseStored as evidence JSON.
The latest amendment winsAn amendment replaces the clause it names.
Supplier comes from the textThe file name isn't trusted.
Regex first, then ClaudeWithout an API key, regex only. Model: claude-sonnet-5-5.
Blank over a guessUnclear fields stay empty for the reviewer.
One review per agreementRequired before its terms value any claim.
Workflow states

From alert to recovered money

Afterlife computes the first three stages. People own the last two. Finance books the money outside the app.

1 · APP

Alert

A part-and-lot cohort's claim rate stepped up.

Supplier quality engineer reviews before the supplier is named
2 · APP

Opportunity

Linked claim cost in the cohort, shown as a range. Never booked.

Shown in the brief draft
3 · APP

Eligible

  • warranty claim, already paid
  • link ≥ recovery threshold, or confirmed
  • single-supplier lot
  • agreement reviewed
  • inside warranty window
  • before filing deadline
Computed per claim
4 · PERSON

Submitted

Filed with the supplier. recovery_status = submitted

Warranty recovery manager
5 · PERSON

Settled

Supplier credit received. recovered_usd > 0

Finance books it

Evaluation gate

Each step is scored on its own against the generated answer keys, so a strong match rate can't hide a weak attribution or a false alert.

CheckTargetToday
Purchase line → part, holdout companiesprecision and recall ≥ 97%97.8–100% (PR #5)
Claim → part, holdout companies≥ 99% precision at the recovery threshold; recall reportedmatch_claims not built
Alert names the right supplier and first lotPrairie and Ironridge, 3 seeds eachsample passes (Keystone, PO-450005-010); generated data waits on generate_claims
Negatives stay quietBluewater never flagged; Northwind 0 alertsBluewater passes on sample; Northwind pending
